letters.notes: waaw. THE rule of the day: waaw/yaa are CONSONANTS (w/y) in 3 cases - (1) at the beginning of a word (waajib), (2) the first of two vowel letters together (jawaab, buyuut), (3) carrying a sukuun (khawkh, thawb) (1001-1648; board t1580/t1610). As a consonant it takes any vowel: 'wa, wu, wi' (1111-1114, 1150-1153). 'It's not u, it's a wa... like the w sound' (1779-1785). Book error she flagged: the book says 'preceded by or followed by' a vowel; she says FOLLOWED by only (3302-3380).

her_clear_utterances.context: 'waaw, because waaw is the first letter of the word' (ar واو)
